# Alert

Figma: [05a. Alert](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-922) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-07

Inline contextual notification with a tone-colored icon, a title, optional description and link, an optional action button chip, and a dismiss control. 30 variants encode 5 tones (info/success/warning/error/neutral) × 3 styles (Filled/Outlined/Plain) × 2 directions (LTR/RTL). 10 properties cover content, visibility toggles, and icon swaps. Use for in-page status messages, action confirmations, validation errors - anywhere the user needs context without leaving the screen.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/alert/reference.png`

### Alert

Inline in-page message with tone icon, title, optional description, link, action chip and close, in Filled, Outlined or Plain style. It sits inside content and persists until dismissed or resolved.

Level: molecule · Contains: Button

Use when:
- Form submission errors at the top of a form (Tone=error)
- Confirmation after an action that stays on screen, such as KYC documents received
- Contextual guidance inside a flow with a Read more link
- Warning with an action chip, such as an expired ID that needs renewal

Don't use when:
- Page-level or account-level announcement with a primary CTA (KYC reminder, maintenance): use Banner
- Brief auto-dismissing confirmation: use Toast
- A decision that must block the screen: use Dialog or Modal
- Help text under one field: use Form Field Helper
- Nothing to show after loading: use EmptyState

Accessibility: Error alerts use role=alert, others role=status; title text states the meaning; keep showClose unless the issue blocks.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Alert is the canonical in-page notification primitive. Use it whenever the user needs status, validation, or contextual help that should NOT leave the current screen. Five tones encode semantic meaning (info, success, warning, error, neutral). Three styles encode visual weight (Filled for high-attention messages, Outlined for medium attention, Plain for inline alerts that should not interrupt). Designers compose meaningful messages by overriding the title, description, link, and button text per instance.

### When to reach for Alert

- Validation errors after a form submission ("Two required fields are missing").
- Confirmation messages after a successful action ("Your KYC documents have been received").
- Contextual help or guidance inside a form or flow ("Tip: complete your profile to unlock premium deals").
- Warnings about destructive or sensitive actions ("Closing this account is permanent").

### When NOT to use Alert

- Brief transient notifications (3-second toast) - use Toast (05b, deferred).
- Full-screen blocking confirmations - use a Modal/Dialog pattern.
- Persistent status next to a single field - use FieldHelper or FieldError patterns.
- Account/profile-level notifications that persist across sessions - use a NotificationCenter pattern.

### Sample tones

### Anatomy

An Alert has up to six elements arranged horizontally. From the leading edge to the trailing edge in LTR: close icon, optional button chip, tone icon, title with optional description and link, all reading left to right. In RTL the order mirrors visually but the data model is the same.

### Elements

- Close icon (closeIcon INSTANCE_SWAP, default Icon/x): tap-to-dismiss control. Always present unless showClose=false.
- Button chip (button frame, controlled by showButton BOOLEAN): a small bordered chip with a tone-colored label. Use sparingly - only when the alert has a clear primary action.
- Tone icon (icon INSTANCE_SWAP): the tone-colored circular icon. Defaults vary per tone (info → Icon/info, success → Icon/check, warning → Icon/alert-triangle, error → Icon/dangerous, neutral → Icon/info). Designers can swap per instance.
- Title (title TEXT): bold, tone-colored. The single most important piece of content. Always present.
- Description (description TEXT, controlled by showDescription BOOLEAN): regular weight, muted color. One sentence of supporting context. Default ON.
- Link (linkText TEXT, controlled by showLink BOOLEAN): semibold, tone-colored. A short call-to-action ("Read more"). Default OFF.

> **Tip:** The Alert defaults to a compact layout: just title + description + close + tone icon. Add the button or link only when the user needs to act on the alert. A noisy Alert with too many controls reads as a banner ad.

### Tones

Five tones convey semantic meaning. Pick the tone based on what the alert MEANS, not what looks nice. The wrong tone is louder than no tone at all.

Tone = info

Default. Use for neutral guidance, contextual help, or status that does not require action ("Your account is being reviewed", "Maintenance scheduled tonight"). The blue says "here is something useful to know".

Tone = success

Use for completion or affirmative confirmation ("KYC complete", "Settlement processed", "Bank details saved"). The green says "this worked".

Tone = warning

Use for issues that need attention but are not blocking ("Documents expire soon", "Profile incomplete"). The amber says "please look at this".

Tone = error

Use for failures or blocking issues ("Upload failed", "Validation failed", "Connection lost"). The red says "this did not work" or "this is broken". Reserve for true errors - overusing diminishes urgency.

Tone = neutral

Use for low-priority messages that should not pull visual attention ("Tip", "Announcement", "Reminder"). The gray says "this is incidental information".

### Styles

Three styles encode visual weight. Same tone, different prominence. Pick by how loud the message should feel relative to the surrounding content.

Style = Filled

Tinted background + tone border. Highest visual weight. Use for primary status messages that need to be the most prominent thing on the screen. The default choice for most product alerts.

Style = Outlined

White background + tone border. Medium visual weight. Use when the Alert sits inside a card or other tinted background where Filled would clash. Also use when you want a slightly more reserved presence.

Style = Plain

No background, no border - just the icon, title, and description on the surrounding canvas. Lowest visual weight. Use for inline alerts in dense content (form-field errors, table-row warnings) where a bordered alert would feel heavy.

### In context - common patterns

Four canonical Safqah patterns showing the Alert in real usage.

### Pattern 1: Form validation error

After the user submits a form with errors, an Alert appears at the top of the form with the error tone. The Alert is dismissible. Use error tone, Filled style for maximum visibility.

### Pattern 2: Success confirmation

After a successful action (KYC approved, settlement processed, deal subscribed), display a success Alert at the top of the screen. Auto-dismiss after a few seconds, or let the user dismiss it. Filled style with success tone.

### Pattern 3: Contextual guidance with link

Inside a form or onboarding flow, show contextual help with showLink=true to point the user to relevant documentation. Use info tone, Outlined style to avoid competing with the form fields.

### Pattern 4: Warning with action button

When the user needs to act on an alert (update expired documents, retry a failed action, review a setting), include the action button chip. Use warning or error tone depending on urgency.

### Properties guide

Alert exposes 10 properties grouped into three families: content (TEXT), visibility (BOOLEAN), and icon swapping (INSTANCE_SWAP). Designers override these per instance to compose meaningful alerts.

### TEXT properties

title  ·  TEXT

Default: "Alert title"

The bold tone-colored title. Always present. Keep it short - one short sentence or fragment. Avoid full punctuation; the body text carries the detail.

description  ·  TEXT

Default: "Description of the alert with context for the reader."

One to two sentences of supporting context. Set to empty string OR toggle showDescription=false to hide.

linkText  ·  TEXT

Default: "Read more"

Short call-to-action like "Read more", "Learn how", "View settings". Only visible when showLink=true.

buttonLabel  ·  TEXT

Default: "Action"

Single-word verb like "Renew", "Retry", "Review". Only visible when showButton=true. Keep under 12 characters to avoid breaking the row layout.

### BOOLEAN properties (visibility toggles)

showDescription  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: true

Toggle the description visibility. Hide for title-only alerts where the title carries the full message.

showLink  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: false

Toggle the link visibility. Use for contextual guidance that points to docs or settings.

showButton  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: false

Toggle the action button chip. Use only when the alert has a clear primary action.

showClose  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: true

Toggle the close X icon. Hide for non-dismissible alerts (e.g. blocking validation errors that must be addressed before continuing).

### INSTANCE_SWAP properties

icon  ·  INSTANCE_SWAP

Default: Icon/info (varies per tone)

The tone-colored leading icon. Defaults are tone-matched: info→Icon/info, success→Icon/check, warning→Icon/alert-triangle, error→Icon/dangerous, neutral→Icon/info. Swap for domain-specific icons (e.g. Icon/user-circle for an account alert).

closeIcon  ·  INSTANCE_SWAP

Default: Icon/x

The dismiss control icon. Almost always Icon/x. Swap only for unusual cases (e.g. a back arrow on a special alert).

### Code examples - Flutter

### Basic usage

```dart
// Default info alert (English, LTR)
const SyntropyAlert(
  tone: AlertTone.info,
  title: 'Alert title',
  description: 'Description of the alert with context for the reader.',
)

// Success alert after KYC approval
const SyntropyAlert(
  tone: AlertTone.success,
  style: AlertStyle.filled,
  title: 'KYC verification complete',
  description: 'Your documents have been approved.',
)

// Error alert that cannot be dismissed (blocking)
const SyntropyAlert(
  tone: AlertTone.error,
  style: AlertStyle.filled,
  title: 'Please fix two errors before submitting',
  description: 'Your IBAN is invalid, and the national ID is required.',
  showClose: false,
)

// Arabic RTL alert
const SyntropyAlert(
  tone: AlertTone.info,
  style: AlertStyle.outlined,
  direction: TextDirection.rtl,
  title: 'عنوان التنبيه',
  description: 'وصف التنبيه مع سياق للقارئ.',
)
```

### With action button and link

```dart
SyntropyAlert(
  tone: AlertTone.warning,
  style: AlertStyle.filled,
  title: 'Your CMA license expires in 30 days',
  description: 'Renew now to maintain access to premium deals.',
  showButton: true,
  buttonLabel: 'Renew',
  onButtonTap: () => Navigator.push(
    context,
    MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const LicenseRenewalPage()),
  ),
  showLink: true,
  linkText: 'Read renewal guide',
  onLinkTap: () => launchUrl(Uri.parse('https://safqah.sa/help/cma-renewal')),
  onClose: () => setState(() => _alertVisible = false),
)
```

### Implementation

```dart
enum AlertTone { info, success, warning, error, neutral }
enum AlertStyle { filled, outlined, plain }

class SyntropyAlert extends StatelessWidget {
  final String title;
  final String? description;
  final String? linkText;
  final String? buttonLabel;
  final AlertTone tone;
  final AlertStyle style;
  final TextDirection direction;
  final bool showClose;
  final VoidCallback? onClose;
  final VoidCallback? onLinkTap;
  final VoidCallback? onButtonTap;

  const SyntropyAlert({
    super.key,
    required this.title,
    this.description,
    this.linkText,
    this.buttonLabel,
    this.tone = AlertTone.info,
    this.style = AlertStyle.filled,
    this.direction = TextDirection.ltr,
    this.showClose = true,
    this.onClose,
    this.onLinkTap,
    this.onButtonTap,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    final tokens = _tokensFor(tone, theme);
    
    return Directionality(
      textDirection: direction,
      child: Container(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: style == AlertStyle.filled ? tokens.bg : (style == AlertStyle.outlined ? theme.bg.surface : null),
          border: style != AlertStyle.plain
            ? Border.all(color: tokens.border, width: 1)
            : null,
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8),
        ),
        child: Row(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            if (showClose) ...[
              IconButton(
                icon: const Icon(SyntropyIcons.x, size: 16),
                onPressed: onClose,
                padding: EdgeInsets.zero,
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
            ],
            Icon(tokens.icon, color: tokens.iconColor, size: 20),
            const SizedBox(width: 12),
            Expanded(
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text(title, style: theme.text.semibold14.copyWith(color: tokens.text)),
                  if (description != null) ...[
                    const SizedBox(height: 4),
                    Text(description!, style: theme.text.regular12.copyWith(color: theme.text.muted)),
                  ],
                  if (linkText != null) ...[
                    const SizedBox(height: 4),
                    GestureDetector(
                      onTap: onLinkTap,
                      child: Text(linkText!, style: theme.text.semibold12.copyWith(color: tokens.text)),
                    ),
                  ],
                ],
              ),
            ),
            if (buttonLabel != null) ...[
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
              _ButtonChip(label: buttonLabel!, tone: tokens, onTap: onButtonTap),
            ],
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Warning:** TEXT property defaults are English. RTL variants in the set ALSO display English in the asset panel preview because of a Figma platform constraint: when a TEXT property is bound, the variant set takes the LAST written characters value as the property default. Workaround: designers override the title/description per instance with Arabic when placing an RTL variant in a real design. The reference frame and doc page demonstrate this correctly.

> **Info:** The 30-variant matrix (Tone × Style × Direction) is intentional. Resist requests to add more tones (e.g. "celebration" or "promotional") without strong evidence. Each additional tone forces designers to make a new decision and dilutes the existing five.

> **Info:** Plain style is for inline alerts in DENSE content only - table rows, form fields, list items. Do NOT use Plain as a default "lightweight" alert. Default to Filled; reach for Outlined when Filled clashes with surroundings; reach for Plain only when even an Outlined border would feel heavy.

> **Tip:** When to use Alert vs Toast vs Modal vs FieldHelper: Alert = in-page status that should be seen but not block; Toast (05b) = brief transient confirmation that auto-dismisses; Modal/Dialog = full attention required, blocks interaction; FieldHelper = persistent help text below a single field.

> **Warning:** The close icon is ALWAYS present unless showClose=false. Accessibility: do not hide the close icon casually. Hide it only when the alert MUST be addressed before continuing (blocking validation, critical system messages). Otherwise, give the user a way out.

> **Info:** buttonLabel becomes a chip when showButton=true. Use the chip SPARINGLY. An Alert with a button is asking the user to act - make sure the action is clear and worth the visual weight. If the action is "Dismiss", use the close X instead.

> **Info:** The legacy Type=Pending tone is renamed to Tone=neutral. If a flow needs a "pending" semantic (e.g. "your request is being processed"), use Tone=info (because it is awaiting an outcome, not neutral). Use Tone=neutral for non-status announcements like maintenance windows.
